name.text: Probability of Selecting Paperback Books from a Shelf

questiontext.text:
\({@n_select@}\) books are taken from a shelf containing \({@n@}\) books of which \({@n_paperback@}\) are paper-back and \({@n_hardcopy@}\) are hard-copy.
Find the probability that the set of \({@n_select@}\) books consists of at least \({@2@}\) paper-back.

Note: Give you answer in exact form or correct to \(3\) decimal places

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

To find the probability that the set of four books consists of at least two paperbacks, we can calculate the probability of selecting sets with two, three, or four paperbacks and then sum them up.

First, let's calculate the total number of ways to choose {@n_select@} books out of {@n@} , which is given by the combination formula:

\( \displaystyle \text{Total number of selection} = ^{@n@} C_{@n_select@} ={@total_outcomes@} \\ \text{Number of selections at least} \, 2 \, \text{paper back} =\left( ^{@n_paperback@} C_2 \times ^{@n_hardcopy@} C_2\right) + \left(^{@n_paperback@} C_3 \times ^{@n_hardcopy@} C_1 \right) + \left(^{@n_paperback@} C_4 \times ^{@n_hardcopy@} C_0 \right)={@favorable_outcomes@} \\ \displaystyle \text{P(Number of selections at least} \, 2 \, \text{paper back})= \frac{{@favorable_outcomes@} }{{@total_outcomes@}}={@ta@} \approx {@decimalplaces(ta,3)@} \)
